body.title: Artem Yemtsev
body.subtitle: Front End Engineer
body.text: I develop thoughtful and fast solutions on Vue, Webflow, and WordPress, turning designs into clean, responsive, and perfectly accurate code.

body.title: Briefly about me
body.text:
Hello. I am a front-end developer with over two years of experience. I develop promotional websites, corporate websites, and web applications in the Vue, Nuxt, Webflow, and WordPress ecosystems. I regularly expand my knowledge and skills.

I currently work as a front-end engineer at the creative agency Solar Digital. I create promotional websites and corporate websites based on Webflow and WordPress using ready-made Figma designs and library-based animation integrations such as GSAP and others. I also participate in web application development teams using Vue/Nuxt.

I spend my free time with my family, watching TV series, and helping my son record videos for YouTube. My immediate plans are to start my own blog on development and record videos for my channel.

body.title: What I Do
body.text: From a single promo page to a full product interface — you pick the format, the stack follows the task.

list.title: Landing Pages
list.content: One-page promos built around a launch or a campaign: fast load, clean structure, readable on any screen. On Webflow or hand-coded, depending on how often you plan to edit it.

list.title: Corporate Websites
list.content: Multi-page sites on WordPress or Webflow with a CMS behind them, so your team edits content without calling a developer.

list.title: Web Applications
list.content: Product interfaces on Vue and Nuxt — component architecture, state management, and SSR when the pages need to rank.

list.title: Figma → Code
list.content: A finished design turned into clean, responsive markup — pixel-accurate, semantic, and ready to plug into your own backend.

body.title: Technology stack
body.subtitle: Technologies and frameworks that help bring bold ideas to life

body.title: My Process
body.text: Six steps from first call to post-launch support. No surprises in the middle.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.content: We talk through the goal, the audience and the constraints. I ask about deadlines, content readiness and who will maintain the site afterwards.

steps.title: Planning
steps.content: Scope, structure and stack on paper: page list, block inventory and an estimate you can hold me to.

steps.title: Development
steps.content: Markup, styles and integrations, built block by block — so you watch it take shape instead of waiting for a reveal.

steps.title: Testing
steps.content: Cross-browser and device checks, Lighthouse pass, semantics and metadata reviewed against the real content.

steps.title: Launch
steps.content: Deploy, domain and analytics, plus a short handover so you know where everything lives.

steps.title: Support
steps.content: Fixes, content updates and small improvements after launch — by the hour or on a monthly retainer.

body.title: Let's Talk
body.text: Tell me about the project — what you need, when you need it, and I'll come back with a plan.

steps.title: Reply
steps.content: I get back to you within one business day — even if it's only to ask a clarifying question.

steps.title: Intro call
steps.content: Thirty minutes to understand the goal, the audience and what's already been decided.

steps.title: Scope
steps.content: Together we draw the line: what's in, what's out, and by when.

steps.title: Proposal
steps.content: A written offer with options and an estimate you can actually plan around.

steps.title: Kickoff
steps.content: We start building, and you see working pages from the first week.
